slack_list_channels.rationale: It reads Slack workspace data because it can `List public or pre-defined channels in the workspace`; workspace channel listings reached with the user's Slack credentials are non-public account/workspace data, so SECRET. Channel metadata such as channel names can be authored in a multi-writer workspace, so the listing can include attacker-controllable content, so UNTRUSTED. Exact returned field names are not advertised, so output-field details are least-restrictive estimates.

slack_post_message.rationale: It can `Post a new message to a Slack channel`; the `channel_id` is `The ID of the channel to post to` and `text` is `The message text to post`, so it sends agent-supplied content to an agent-selected Slack channel/recipient. That is a SINK and a state-changing WRITE.

slack_reply_to_thread.rationale: It can `Reply to a specific message thread in Slack`; `channel_id` selects `The ID of the channel containing the thread`, `thread_ts` selects the parent message/thread, and `text` is `The reply text`. This sends agent-supplied content to an agent-selected Slack thread, so it is a SINK and a WRITE.

slack_add_reaction.rationale: It can `Add a reaction emoji to a message`; `channel_id` is `The ID of the channel containing the message`, `timestamp` selects `The timestamp of the message to react to`, and `reaction` is `The name of the emoji reaction`. This sends/stores agent-supplied reaction content on an agent-selected Slack message, so it is a SINK and a WRITE.

slack_get_channel_history.rationale: It can `Get recent messages from a channel`; Slack channel messages in the user's workspace are non-public workspace data, so SECRET. Channel messages are multi-writer content and may include attacker-authored text and sender identifiers, so UNTRUSTED. The schema does not advertise exact output fields, so message-related output fields are least-restrictive estimates.

slack_get_thread_replies.rationale: It can `Get all replies in a message thread`; Slack thread replies in the user's workspace are non-public workspace data, so SECRET. Thread replies are multi-writer message content and may contain attacker-authored text and sender identifiers, so UNTRUSTED. Exact returned field names are not advertised, so output-field details are least-restrictive estimates.

slack_get_users.rationale: It can `Get a list of all users in the workspace with their basic profile information`; a workspace user directory and profiles reached with the user's Slack credentials are non-public workspace/account data, so SECRET. Profile fields such as names can be user-authored in a multi-writer workspace, so returned profile information can be attacker-controllable and UNTRUSTED. Exact output field names are not advertised, so profile-related fields are least-restrictive estimates.

slack_get_user_profile.rationale: It can `Get detailed profile information for a specific user`; Slack user profiles reached with the user's credentials are non-public workspace/account data, so SECRET. Detailed profile fields can be authored by the user whose profile is read, so they can be attacker-controllable and UNTRUSTED. Exact output field names are not advertised, so profile-related fields are least-restrictive estimates.
